the time-dependent behavior of polymers is caused by the slippage of chains in the network and that the slippage rate depends on the number of chains in the contact area between two neighboring chains, which in turn depends on the deformation of the network.

the rheology of crosslinked polymers is controlled by the slippage of chains, that this slippage is caused by the motion of chain ends in the crosslinks, and that the motion of chain end is controlled by the local stress and the local strain.
